source.title: Neural Scaling Laws Surpass Chemical Accuracy for the Many-Electron Schr\"odinger Equation
source.authors: D. Jiang; Xue-Lan Wen; Yi-Xiao Chen; Rui-Chen Li; Wei-Zhong Fu; Hung Q. Pham; Ji Chen; Di He; W. Goddard; Li-Wei Wang; Wei-Luo Ren

record.file_problem: The paper and supplementary information are present. Some equations and symbols are garbled in the extracted text, but the scaling results relevant here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests neural-network scaling in ab initio quantum chemistry, a different training setting and target from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling results for neural-network wavefunction energy errors, not language-model held-out cross-entropy. It does not report language-model results or a fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep.
record.test_reason: Fits power laws of neural-network wavefunction energy error (the variational training objective) against parameter count and GPU time in ab initio quantum chemistry. This is a new training regime, so it bears on V5 only. Model sizes span about two orders of magnitude (2.6e5 to 2.3e7 parameters for benzene).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with three additions. The authors attribute the systematic power-law decay of energy error with model size and compute specifically to the LAVA optimizer. They state that standard NNVMC scales worse and tends to saturate. They claim the resulting extrapolated energies reach sub-kJ/mol accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Applies scaling analysis to LAVA-optimized neural-network wavefunctions and molecular energy errors, rather than language-model pretraining and held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported scaling behavior varies by system and optimization method: LAVA shows clearer scaling than NNVMC on the tested cyclobutadiene and ozone cases; the cyclobutadiene barrier also fluctuates initially as network size increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Runtime scales as Ne^2.1 at fixed model size and Ne^5.3 to keep chemical accuracy, as the number of electrons grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute cost of NN wavefunctions scales polynomially with system size at fixed target accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Energy is linear in local-energy variance across model sizes (average OLS r2 > 0.99); this relation is used for extrapolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance-energy linearity across model scales enables zero-variance extrapolation.

record.problems: The study concerns quantum-chemistry wavefunction energy errors, not language-model cross-entropy. Several scaling trends are presented as plots without tabulated numerical fit values; the authors report an aggregate fit statistic for 11 systems but not a per-system list of fit statistics in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Supplementary scaling plots for additional molecular systems and network configurations are not individually transcribed where the text gives no numerical values or explicitly named per-condition results; see Supplementary Figures 1–4, 7–10, 11–12, 14–17. The corresponding textual aggregate result is recorded in r1.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No validated extrapolation of small-run fits to much larger runs. The fits are used to estimate the resources needed, but those predictions are not checked against actual runs.
Effect of shape at fixed parameter count. Width and depth are co-varied with size, not compared at fixed size.
Image and video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Data or step scaling is not tested separately from parameter count.
Effect of fitting, counting or schedule choices on the exponents for language models.

missing.what: LAVA versus NNVMC scaling comparison: NNVMC has worse power-law scaling on cyclobutadiene and no good power law on the ozone open-ring minimum.
Power law of local-energy variance versus parameter count, average r2 > 0.97 across systems.
missing.locator: Methods 4.3 eq. 21; Supp Note 2; Supp Fig 2

missing.what: Per-system r2 and exponent distributions across all systems.

record.verdict_notes: V5 linkage is a stretch, because this is unsupervised variational optimization of a wavefunction, not data-driven training. However, the energy is the training loss and the authors frame the work explicitly as neural scaling laws citing Kaplan et al. For ozone, cyclobutadiene and N2, errors are measured relative to LAVA-SE, which is extrapolated from the same runs, so those fits are partly circular. Only the 11 systems with experimental references (r1, r9) give an independent test. The exponent is system-dependent. The reader's limits_scope label based on the fluctuating cyclobutadiene barrier is dropped, because the barrier is not the scaled quantity.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from fits to smaller language-model runs.
The loss-minimising allocation of language-model parameters and tokens at fixed compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests neural wavefunction energy-error scaling in molecular quantum chemistry only; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations under different counting, schedule, data, or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: LAVA-optimized neural-network wavefunctions (LapNet), energy error versus parameter count, about 2.6e5 to 2.3e7 parameters
relationships.reason: Benzene error vs experiment scales as Np^-0.52 (r9). The average log-log OLS r2 exceeds 0.95 across 11 systems with experimental references (r1). Ozone and N2 show power-law decay, though measured against the extrapolated reference (r26–r29).
relationships.display_finding: Benzene error scaled with parameter exponent −0.52, average log-log regression R² exceeded 0.95 across 11 experimentally referenced systems, and ozone and N2 showed power-law decay against extrapolated references.

relationships.condition: Standard NNVMC optimizer (LapNet baseline) instead of LAVA
relationships.reason: Based on the text, with no row capturing it: Supp Note 2.1 reports NNVMC scales significantly worse on cyclobutadiene and fails to give a good power law on the ozone open-ring minimum. The main text says scaling NN wavefunctions usually saturates without LAVA. So the power law depends on the optimizer.
relationships.display_finding: Standard NNVMC scaled substantially worse on cyclobutadiene and failed to produce a good power law for the ozone open-ring minimum, while neural-wavefunction scaling generally saturated without LAVA.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Energy error follows reported power-law trends with model size across the tested systems; the benzene exponent and the aggregate fit statistic are stated in r1 and r9, with individual benzene scale measurements in r2–r8 and additional system results in r26–r29.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cyclobutadiene automerization barrier across the listed network configurations
reader_labels.reason: The barrier initially fluctuates and only decreases more clearly at larger sizes, rather than following a uniformly monotonic trend in the reported values (r18–r25).
